Note::keep_printable¶

Back to Note API Reference

Signature¶

Note Note::keep_printable() const

Keep Only The Visible ASCII Range In Every Cell¶

keep_printable() returns a new Note, same shape as the input, keeping only bytes in the printable ASCII range 0x20–0x7E (space through ~). Everything else is deleted: all ASCII control bytes — including tab (\t) and newline (\n) — and every non-ASCII byte. Use it to sanitize text for a single-line log field, a terminal display, or a format that rejects control characters.

Note that tab and newline are removed, not converted to spaces, so "line1\tcol2\nline2" collapses to "line1col2line2". If you need to keep line structure, split first (split_lines) or normalise whitespace before calling this.

keep_printable is shape-preserving, cell-independent, and returns a fresh Note.

Example 1: Control Bytes Are Removed¶

std::cout << pluss::note::print(
    pluss::make_note({"line1\tcol2\nline2", "clean"}).keep_printable())
    << "\n";

Output¶

Note(shape=[2], dim=1, numel=2, encoding=utf8)
["line1col2line2", "clean"]

Example 2: Non-ASCII Is Removed Too¶

const pluss::Note n = pluss::make_note({"café — ok"}).keep_printable();
std::cout << n << "\n";

Output¶

Note(shape=[1], dim=1, numel=1, encoding=utf8)
["caf  ok"]

The é and the em dash are non-ASCII, so their bytes are dropped, leaving the surrounding spaces.

See Also¶

  • Note::keep_ascii: keeps ASCII control bytes; only non-ASCII is dropped.

  • pluss::coden::Note::remove_control_chars: drop controls but keep non-ASCII text.

  • Note::remove_symbols: keep letters, digits, and whitespace (including non-ASCII).
